;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Sinai insurgency]]
**Fourteen people are killed after bombs planted by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Sinai Province|Islamic State]] militants explode near civilian homes in [[Bir al-Abd]], [[Egypt]]. The bombs were placed when militants attacked several villages in the town in July, forcing people to flee their homes, who then returned a month later when [[Egyptian Army|soldiers]] secured the area. [https://apnews.com/article/egypt-africa-a1ef2bfa5fdb1744717cc90e76847af1 (Associated Press)]
*[[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
**[[Azerbaijan]]i [[Azerbaijani Armed Forces|troops]] continue to advance inside [[Nagorno-Karabakh]], capturing the town of [[Qubadlı]], the administrative capital of [[Qubadli District]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/azerbaijan-front-line/azerbaijan-liberates-qubadlis-city-center-from-occupation/2018846 (Anadolu Angency)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Cardinals created by Francis]]
**[[Pope Francis]] announces the creation of 13 new [[Cardinal (Catholic Church)|cardinals]], including the elevation of [[Archbishop]] [[Wilton Daniel Gregory|Wilton Gregory]] of Washington who will become the first [[African-American]] cardinal in the [[Roman Catholic Church]]. The elevation is scheduled to occur on November 28. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/pope-cardinal-gregory-dc/2020/10/25/5a24cfe4-16b5-11eb-8bda-814ca56e138b_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

;Business and economy
*The [[Lahore Metro|Metro]] of [[Lahore]], [[Pakistan]], opens to the public. [https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/25-Oct-2020/punjab-cm-inaugurates-lahore-s-much-delayed-orange-line-metro-train (''Daily Pakistan'')]

;Health and environment 
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria]]
****[[Prime Minister of Bulgaria|Prime Minister]] [[Boyko Borisov]] tests positive for [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-10-25/bulgarian-premier-tests-positive-for-covid-recovering-at-home (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] registers a record 52,010 new confirmed infections over the past 24 hours, according to a statement from the [[Minister of Health (France)|health ministry]], taking the nationwide total to 1,138,507 and becoming the world's fifth highest number of cases after the [[United States]], [[India]], [[Brazil]] and [[Russia]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/france-hits-record-52-010-daily-covid-cases-spain-declares-n1244709 (NBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****In an agreement with regional authorities, [[Italy]]'s [[Conte II Cabinet|Giuseppe Conte government]] orders cinemas, swimming pools, and gyms to close tomorrow in a further attempt to curb the rapid rise in COVID-19 cases. Bars and restaurants will have to close by 6:00 p.m. local time. The new rules will last until November 24. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/italy-coronavirus-restrictions-early-curfews-cafes-restaurants-covid19-pandemic-2020-10-25/ (CBS News)]
****The number of confirmed cases in Italy reaches a new record of 21,273 cases in the last 24 hours. It is the first time that daily new cases have surpassed 20,000 since the pandemic began. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/coronavirus-europe-italy-second-wave-lockdown/2020/10/25/6c011306-16df-11eb-82db-60b15c874105_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] registers a record of 3,149 new cases in the past 24 hours, taking the nationwide total of cases since the [[pandemic]] began to 59,247. [https://hungarytoday.hu/covid-hungary-sunday-new-cases-record/ (''Hungary Today'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The number of new infections in the [[Netherlands]] jumped by 10,203 cases in the past 24 hours, hitting a new record not seen since the beginning of the pandemic, according to data released by the [[National Institute for Public Health and the Environment]] (RIVM). [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-netherlands-tally/coronavirus-cases-in-the-netherlands-hit-new-record-up-by-more-than-10000-idINKBN27A0IT?il=0 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Prime Minister of Spain|Prime Minister]] [[Pedro Sánchez]] declares a second nationwide "state of alarm" (known as state of emergency) to allow regional authorities to set different hours for the [[curfew]]s as long as they are stricter, close regional borders to travel, and limit gatherings to six people not in the same household. The nationwide curfew begins between 11:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. local time, except in the [[Canary Islands]]. The emergency decree can be extended from an initial 15 days to six months depending on parliamentary approval. [https://www.euronews.com/2020/10/25/coronavirus-spain-prepares-to-declare-state-of-emergency-to-allow-regional-curfews (Euronews)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[Reserve Bank of India]]'s [[List of governors of the Reserve Bank of India|Governor]] [[Shaktikanta Das]] tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/coronavirus-rbi-governor-shaktikanta-das-tests-positive-for-covid-19/article32940504.ece (''The Hindu'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Yang di-Pertuan Agong]] [[Abdullah of Pahang|King Al-Sultan Abdullah]] rejects a proposal by embattled [[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Muhyiddin Yassin]] to declare a [[state of emergency]] to fight a surge of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.kompas.com/global/read/2020/10/25/195241370/raja-malaysia-tidak-perlu-berlakukan-keadaan-darurat-di-tengah-lonjakan (''Kompas'')] [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/malaysias-king-rejects-pms-proposal-declare-emergency-73815317 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]]n authorities increase the COVID-19-related curfew zones to 56 [[Sri Lanka Police|police]] divisions to control the spread of the virus through community-level transmission. [https://www.newindianexpress.com/world/2020/oct/25/sri-lanka-increases-coronavirus-curfew-zones-after-spike-in-cases-2214865.html (''The New Indian Express'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Premier of Victoria|Victorian Premier]] [[Daniel Andrews]] announces the easing of restrictions on gyms, religious gatherings, indoor swimming pools, and other facilities in Regional Victoria effective October 27 at 11:59 p.m. [[Australian Eastern Daylight Time|AEDT]]. He delays an announcement about easing restrictions in [[Melbourne]] pending the outcome of tests connected to an outbreak in the northern suburbs. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-10-25/victoria-coronavirus-daniel-andrews-announces-melbourne-steps/12811116 (ABC Australia)]
***It is announced that [[Tasmania]] will reopen to much of [[Mainland Australia]], which was deemed as "low-risk" states, and [[New Zealand]] tomorrow. The state was the first Australian jurisdiction to close its borders in March and has not recorded a case in more than 70 days. [https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/6983542/tasmania-poised-to-open-borders/?cs=14231 (''The Canberra Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
****[[Ontario]] reports 1,042 new cases, a new record since the start of the outbreak, bringing the total number of cases in the [[provinces and territories of Canada|province]] to 70,373. [https://globalnews.ca/news/7420771/ontario-coronavirus-cases-oct-25-covid19/amp/ (Global News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec]]
****[[Quebec]] surpasses 100,000 cases of COVID-19, becoming the first province in [[Canada]] to hit the milestone since the pandemic began in March. [https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/2020/10/25/canadian-press-newsalert-quebec-reaches-more-than-100000-total-cases-of-covid-19.html (''The Star'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
**Dozens of [[far-right]] protesters in [[Rome]] clash with [[riot police]] during a demonstration against COVID-19 restrictions when 200 masked militants belonging to [[Forza Nuova]] hurl flares and [[firecracker]]s at [[law enforcement in Italy|police]]. Police arrest seven protesters and reported two officers injured. [https://www.trtworld.com/europe/far-right-protesters-clash-with-italian-police-over-new-covid-19-measures-40878 (TRT World)]
**More than 2,000 people protest in [[Naples]] in the evening against the announced measures. [https://www.ilmessaggero.it/italia/napoli_protesta_dpcm_covid_oggi_25_ottobre_cosa_succede_news-5545767.html (''Il Messaggero'')]
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**British [[Special Boat Service]] (SBS) special forces storm the [[Liberia]]n-registered ''Nave Andromeda'' after the tanker was suspected to be [[Maritime hijacking|hijacked]] by a group of [[Nigeria]]n [[stowaway]]s off the [[Isle of Wight]]. The 22 crew members were found safe, and the seven suspected hijackers have been detained by British authorities following a 10-hour stand-off. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-hampshire-54687379 (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2020/oct/29/seven-men-bailed-following-suspected-hijack-of-oil-tanker (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Elections in Canada]]
**[[2020 British Columbia general election]]
***[[Premier of British Columbia]] [[John Horgan]] is projected to win a majority of seats for the [[British Columbia New Democratic Party|New Democratic Party]]; he is the first BC NDP leader to be reelected in the province's history. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/bc-election-results-2020-1.5776058 (CBC)] [https://vancouversun.com/news/local-news/bc-election-2020-live-results (Vancouver Sun)] [https://bc.ctvnews.ca/ctv-news-declares-ndp-majority-in-b-c-election-1.5159102 (CTV)]
*[[2020 Seychellois general election]]
**In an upset election, [[Wavel Ramkalawan]] is declared the winner after defeating incumbent [[Danny Faure]] of the ruling [[United Seychelles]] party, which has been in power since the 1970s. The liberal candidate received 54% of votes cast to win the election. [https://apnews.com/article/seychelles-wavel-ramkalawan-elections-kenya-indian-ocean-f0b3b5de09f93bf1609580e4f9681a38 (AP)]
*[[2020 Lithuanian parliamentary election]]
**[[Lithuania]] holds the second round of [[Elections in Lithuania|parliamentary elections]] amidst an economic crisis due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Lithuania|COVID-19 pandemic]]. The first round was held on October 11. [https://www.stcatharinesstandard.ca/ts/news/world/europe/2020/10/25/lithuania-holds-parliamentary-vote-as-pandemic-hits-jobs.html (''The Standard'')]
*[[2020 Chilean national plebiscite]]
**A [[referendum]] to start the process to draft a new constitution is held in Chile. The referendum was one of the announcements made after the [[2019–20 Chilean protests]]. Over 78% vote in favour of abandoning the [[Chilean Constitution of 1980|1980 Constitution]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20201025-from-protest-to-ballot-box-chile-votes-in-referendum-for-change (France 24)]
*[[2019–2021 Iraqi protests]]
**Thousands of [[Iraq]]is take to the streets in [[Baghdad]] and major southern cities, including [[Basra]] and [[Najaf]], to both mark the anniversary of the protests and renew calls to end [[Corruption in Iraq|corruption]]. Security forces in central Baghdad threw [[tear gas]] to prevent marchers from crossing strategic bridges, injuring at least six, and around 43 officers were injured after protesters threw [[Molotov cocktail]]s at them. [https://apnews.com/article/baghdad-iraq-middle-east-6794a4d2c0594f921dc4c74b5e3d0f3b (AP)]
*[[Crisis in Venezuela during the Bolivarian Revolution]]
**[[Venezuela]]n opposition leader [[Leopoldo López]] arrives to [[Madrid]], [[Spain]], after spending the last year in the Spanish embassy to avoid [[house arrest]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/25/venezuelan-opposition-politician-leopoldo-lopez-arrives-in-madrid (Al Jazeera)]

**In [[association football|football]], former [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] player [[Ronaldinho]] tests positive for COVID-19 and is in self-quarantine. **The [[Tennessee Titans]] are fined [[United States dollar|$]]350,000 for violating the [[National Football League|NFL]]'s COVID-19 protocols. [https://www.abc12.com/2020/10/25/ap-source-nfl-fines-titans-350000-for-covid-19-outbreak-2/ (Associated Press via WJRT-TV)]
